Dangling-reference repairs: none needed. Each referring phrase finds its referent earlier in the note. "This subject" points to inductive logic. "Their great use" and "They are only" point to the theories in the sentence before. "This wave of scientific logic" points to the tendency the preceding statements describe. "These teachers" and "they say" point to Schiller and Dewey. "This general conception of all truth" points to the instrumental view stated just before. "These other sciences" points to geology, biology and philology in the previous statement.

Mid-sentence cut (illustration, not a dangling-reference repair): in "In the establishment of these other sciences…", I removed the dash-enclosed examples ("--as denudation by weather, say, or variation from parental type, or change of dialect by incorporation of new words and pronunciations--"). This leaves two quotes joined by {}.

"We"/"you" judged generic and left unrepaired: "our time", "our sciences", "our laws", "we write our reports of nature", "our ideas and beliefs", "OUR EXPERIENCE", "HELP US", "we can ride", "carry us", "our experience". All of these mean people, or inquirers, in general.

Dropped statements:
- The sentences elaborating the old theological view of laws, from "His mind also thundered and reverberated in syllogisms" through "…we seize his mind in its very literal intention". These are illustration of the kept statement about men believing they had deciphered the thoughts of the Almighty.
- "If I mention the names of Sigwart, Mach, Ostwald, Pearson, Milhaud, Poincare, Duhem, Ruyssen, those of you who are students will easily identify the tendency I speak of, and will think of additional names." This is illustration (a roll of names) and states no proposition.

No asides.
